title: Factor Theory, Fama-French and Style

maps.tested: Reported both as a named topic ('factor theory') and as a comparison question ('comparison CAPM and multifactor'). Style analysis appears as a standalone theory item.
maps.specifics: One handwritten source writes 'Portfolio Composition (SML, HML)'. This is almost certainly a transcription error for SMB, the Fama-French size factor, not SML, the security market line. Studying the SML here would be studying the wrong object. Also reported: 'investing style theory question'. Value and momentum comparison (LO 84.e) and the low-risk / volatility anomaly (Reading 85) sit adjacent.

vardeezReading: IM-1: Important ("CAPM assumptions and limitations; CAPM vs multifactor models"). IM-2: untiered, with the note "LO 84.C is Imp and LO 84. E is imp which is value vs momentum strategies". IM-3: Very Important ("Grinold's Fundamental Law (IC, Breadth, IR); Calculation of FAMA French Model using SMB, HML (Pls know this very well); Style Analysis").

los.vardeez: Fama-French with SMB and HML: know very well

selectors.name: Trap: SMB vs SML, Fama-French composition
selectors.what: Fama-French portfolio composition: what SMB (small minus big) and HML (high minus low book-to-market) are, how the loadings s and h and the market beta translate into a benchmark of T-bills, market, small, large, value and growth positions, and the planted confusion of SMB with SML, the security market line (the CAPM pricing line, not a factor). Includes the Fama-French expected return or alpha from given loadings: r - rf = alpha + beta(rm - rf) + s SMB + h HML.
selectors.theory: SMB and HML are tradeable long-short factor-mimicking portfolios (USD 1 long, USD 1 short); s > 0 means small-stock tilt, s < 0 large; h > 0 value, h < 0 growth; the market and the average stock have zero s and h and a beta of one; the benchmark puts (1 - beta) in T-bills and beta in the market.

selectors.name: Investing style as a theory item
selectors.what: Theory question on investing style: style, investment and dynamic factors as interchangeable terms (smart beta, alternative beta), static factors held long against dynamic factors that need constant trading, and hedge funds or private equity as bundles of dynamic factors.

selectors.name: Value vs momentum: return and risk
selectors.what: Compare value and momentum: value is robust and a negative-feedback, stabilizing strategy with rational and behavioral explanations; momentum (WML or UMD) earns far more, is a positive-feedback, destabilizing strategy prone to crashes, with mainly behavioral explanations; the two are not opposites (correlation about -16%). Also the swap of robustness profiles of size, value and momentum.

selectors.name: Low-risk anomaly: volatility vs beta
selectors.what: The low-risk anomaly: the volatility anomaly (high idiosyncratic volatility earns low returns) against the beta anomaly (flat average returns across beta quintiles but falling Sharpe ratios), the BAB and VOL factors, and the explanations (data mining, leverage constraints, agency problems, lottery preferences, disagreement with short-sale limits), none of which covers the whole anomaly.

selectors.name: CAPM vs multifactor models
selectors.source: Map: reported as a comparison question ('comparison CAPM and multifactor'); Vardeez: 'CAPM vs multifactor models'
selectors.what: Compare and contrast the CAPM (one factor, the market; beta pricing) with multifactor models (several factors, such as Fama-French size, value and momentum), including the SDF view of the CAPM as a special case.

selectors.name: Style analysis (Sharpe)
selectors.source: Map: 'Style analysis appears as a standalone theory item'; Vardeez: 'Style analysis'
selectors.what: Sharpe style analysis: a benchmark built from tradeable low-cost funds with weights summing to one, estimated over a rolling window (about 60 months), with or without a no-shorting constraint; it handles time-varying factor exposures and the non-tradeable factor portfolios of Fama-French regressions.

selectors.name: CAPM assumptions and limitations
selectors.what: The assumptions of the CAPM (financial wealth only, mean-variance utility, single period, homogeneous expectations, no taxes or transaction costs, price takers, costless information) and where it fails empirically.

selectors.name: Managing volatility risk
selectors.what: Methods of mitigating volatility risk (buying protection through puts or volatility swaps, holding more bonds, selling out-of-the-money puts for the premium) and the challenges of managing it (negative price of risk, short-volatility losses in crises, rebalancing as a short-volatility strategy).

notSelected: IM-1 a (factor theory and risk premiums), IM-1 e (stochastic discount factors), IM-1 f (efficient market theory), IM-2 a (value investing and the value premium, except as part of S3), IM-2 b (macroeconomic risk factors) and IM-3 c (benchmark choice for alpha), IM-3 g (alpha for nonlinear strategies) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
